post.description: Idempotency-Key is required and scoped to the authenticated user. The canonical request body is fingerprinted. A replay returns the original 201 response and conversation id without repeating side effects; a changed body returns 422 idempotency_key_reused and a key used on another route returns 409 idempotency_route. The conversation and key record commit atomically. Records expire after the configured idempotency retention (24 hours by default). delete.summary: Delete a task: gone at once, its data purged within minutes
delete.description: Owner only. The task answers 404 to every read, stream, files call and action from the delete on, and an open event stream ends; its runtime token is revoked and one content-free audit record is written. Its events, stored outputs, held messages and run snapshots are purged in the background within minutes; its workspace and files stay, and its usage still counts for its owner. Deleting a task already deleted answers 204 again and records nothing, until it is purged; then 404. A create retried with the same Idempotency-Key after the task is purged makes a new task.

post.description: Only accepted actions are cached. The canonical request body must match for key replay; a changed body returns 422 idempotency_key_reused. Default retention is 24 hours from acceptance; queued actions remain until delivered or failed. Acceptance persists the queued frame before 202. Replay preserves the original response body; the execution header reports its current status. A new attempt requires a new key. When no slot is free the message is still accepted (202) and waits in a queue that is fair across users; the stream reports session.ready with state queued and queue.ahead until it starts. queue.reason says why: slot (no free sandbox slot) or workspace (another task holds the workspace write lease; with busy_policy = wait it starts when that task's run ends). 429 remains only for the per-conversation action queue bound. A message sent while the task's run is in progress waits on the gateway (held: true) and goes out when the run ends; every message held meanwhile goes out as one user turn, texts joined in order with a blank line. A run that fails or is stopped drops them (see /messages/queued).

post.description: The MCP proxy (ADR-0031), streamable HTTP with JSON answers: one JSON-RPC 2.0 message or a batch of at most 32, at most 1 MiB. Only a runtime token from its own sandbox's address is accepted, and only for a connector in the conversation's connector set. Only initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list, tools/call and notifications/cancelled pass; anything else, or a tools/call for a tool the connector's filter hides, is answered here with a JSON-RPC error. The proxy injects the user's own credential or the connector's shared one, reaches the remote only at checked addresses without following redirects, and filters tools/list answers. An event-stream answer is relayed event by event (each at most 1 MiB; tools/list results filtered). At most 4 calls from a conversation to a connector, and 256 through the proxy, are in flight (429 connector_busy). The remote's Mcp-Session-Id never reaches the runtime: the proxy returns an opaque id bound to the conversation, the connector and the credential source (at most 8 per conversation, 10 minutes idle). A tools/call the runtime abandons is cancelled at the remote with notifications/cancelled. A connector call that fails reaches the task's transcript as a tool error whose code is one of this proxy's refusals, or the runtime's own: `mcp_error` (the server answered with a JSON-RPC error), `mcp_method_not_found` (JSON-RPC -32601) or `mcp_server_exited` (a tool server stopped during the call).

Take over belongs to the socket and ends when it closes. A request without a session or with a wrong Origin is refused before the upgrade (401, 403). Every other refusal upgrades and closes at once, before any screen data, with an application close code and the error code as the reason: 4403 forbidden, 4404 not_found, 4409 no_desktop, screen_viewers or sandbox_not_running (the task has no sandbox starting or live, also when it stops while open); a bridge that drops or doesn't come within 35 s while the sandbox lives (its runtime's link up, or redialling after a restart) closes 4409 screen_unavailable, which the page retries. A second tab's take_over while another holds the screen is refused without closing: it gets control{holder: other} again. Any other close code is a dropped connection.

SecretRead.description: Reads of a secret by one consumer for one conversation, user and run, with one outcome, counted. Never a value, a hash or a length.

consumer.description: The route or connector name; push for a Git credential; host:port for a host key.

user_id.description: The user it was read for; only in the administrator's view.

outcome.description: ok, or why it was refused. absent and unavailable for a stored secret; the host outcomes of ADR-0037 §8 and its Amendment 1 for a host key.

next.description: Pass as before for the next page; null on the last page.

consumers.description: Replaces the whole list; duplicates are removed.

role.description: The caller's role; null for an administrator or a member conversation's owner who isn't a member.

name.description: A user's email; a conversation's agent profile display name.

title.description: A conversation's title, only for its owner (titles are content, SEC-044: never for an administrator).

run_status.description: An agent member's run, from the lifecycle projection (GW-I-113); present only for kind conversation. A run that started and never ended (a crash) reads running, as on the conversation page. A client shows an unknown value as plain words.

can_open.description: Whether the caller may open this agent member's task page: true for the task's owner and for an administrator (who gets its private view), false otherwise. Present only for kind conversation.

ChannelMessageBody.description: A channel message's typed body (ADR-0014 point 3; tqa-types).

author.description: Accepted and ignored: the author is the caller (SEC-015).

limit.description: How many claimants it takes; all resolved to the voting members.

truncated.description: The endpoint offers more models than the 500 listed

excerpt.description: A short redacted excerpt of the upstream answer; never a credential

detail.description: What was wrong with the answer itself, redacted: for models_unreadable, why the list could not be read. Absent otherwise

protocol.description: decision_v1: the relay forwards decision/v1 as is; typed_questions_v1: the relay asks the engine's service one multiple-choice question per step (before steps only) and answers with the decision.

display_name.description: What people read; no control characters or surrounding spaces. The name stays the identifier.

url.description: decision_v1: the engine's base URL; the relay posts to <url>/v1/before_step and /v1/after_response. typed_questions_v1: the service's endpoint, posted to as is. https, with a host; no user information, no fragment, and no credential-like query keys.

scheme.description: How the gateway sends the engine's credential.

header.description: For the header scheme only: Authorization, X-Api-Key, or an X- name of letters, digits and -.

key_ref.description: The installation's credential for the engine: a shared secret that allows the engine (never a user's own). Needs an auth scheme.

timeout_ms.description: How long the engine has to answer.

exposure.description: What the engine sees: tool names only (none), names and arguments (calls), or the full conversation (full). Every change is audited as its own action.

version.description: The version read; absent to create.

model.description: A typed-question engine's model identifier, which its service requires (see the service's documentation); pinned for a measurement. Not accepted on a decision_v1 engine.

min_confidence.description: A typed-question engine's threshold: a choice below it takes the conversation's own route; 0.6 when unset. Not accepted on a decision_v1 engine.

route_hints.description: A typed-question engine's one-line description of each route, offered with its option; the route's name otherwise. Not accepted on a decision_v1 engine.

calls.description: At most this many consultations per period.

tokens.description: At most this many tokens per period, as the service reports them (input and output). Typed-question engines only.

period.description: total: since the budget was set or last changed, so saving a new budget starts a new count; month: the calendar month in UTC, whatever changed in it.

budget.description: The engine's optional budget, an administrator's setting, off when absent; calls or tokens (or both). Counted from the engine's usage rows.

message_id.description: The message's id, for the queue's list and cancel.

held.description: True when the message waits for the task's run to end (send after this).

state.description: waiting_for_slot: a message not behind a run that has not gone out yet (the task waits for a slot or its sandbox is starting); it can be cancelled like a held one.

reason.description: Why a dropped message was dropped.

sent_at.description: When a sent message went out.

after.description: The reader's place in the team's log: the waiting messages come after it.

team_wake.description: Set on the gateway's wake of an agent team's reader (protocol revision 13's marker): a client shows its notice, never the text as the person's message, and offers no Cancel.

lead_brief.description: Set on an agent team member's first turn, with its lead's brief (protocol revision 12): a client shows the gateway's notice, never the text as the person's message, and offers no Cancel.

id.description: The image ID (`sha256:…`): the pin an environment made from it uses.

tags.description: Its local tags; empty for an untagged image.

runtime.description: Whether it holds a runtime this version can run (its protocol-revision label): `too_old` needs a rebuild.

environment.description: The environment it says it is (its `org.tensorquay.environment` label); null without one.

display_name.description: Its label's name for people; null without one.

capabilities.description: The capabilities its label names, as written (an unknown one included); empty without the label.

capabilities_valid.description: False when the capability label names no capability or an unknown one.

usable.description: Whether an environment can be made from it.

reason.description: Plain words: why it is not usable ("too old for this version: rebuild it", "there is no TensorQuay runtime in it", "its capability label names no capability", "its capability label names an unknown capability: gpu"), or, for a built-in that is not added, why ("deleted by an administrator", "not added: an environment named Workstation already exists", "not added: the gateway's configuration file has its own Data environment", "Workstation moves to this build at the gateway's next start", "not added yet: it is added at the gateway's next start"). based_on.description: The built-in whose label it carries without being it (an image built FROM Workstation inherits its labels, or an earlier build): shown as "derived from Workstation". It can be picked for a new environment and never replaces the built-in.

used_by.description: The environments pinned to it, by name.

sandboxes.description: How many tasks' sandboxes run it now.

built_in.description: For a built-in's image (the one its canonical tag `tqa-runtime:<name>` names, its label agreeing): `registered` when it is in the environments, `not_added` when not (the reason says why; an administrator adds it as an environment from here). Null for every other image.

host.description: An exact name, *.domain, or * (any website, only from open_web).

applied.description: How many of its rules are in the allow-list as it put them there: all, some (others were changed, removed or were already the administrator's), or none.

shared.description: false: the viewer's own key; true: a shared key.

last_use.description: The viewer's most recent use they may see, or null.

Only the task's own person gets every field; anyone else (an administrator's listing) gets role, id, state, and for a lead helpers and attention, for a member lead.id: never a name, the lead's title, a helper state or a question.

helpers.description: A lead's helpers now; deleted ones are not counted.

attention.description: How many of the lead's helpers are stuck and failed while the team runs; 0 and 0 once it is stopping or ended, since nothing in it waits on anyone.

waiting_for_you.description: A lead's person_question is unanswered (the task's own person only).

title.description: The lead task's title (its own person only).

name.description: A member's name (its own person only).

can_stop.description: Whether its person's Stop helper would stop it now: while the team runs, any helper but a stopped one or one that couldn't start (a member's own person only).

agent_teams.description: The install switch [agent_teams] enabled, read at start.

TeamMessage.description: A stored agent-team message in the read shape (ADR-0034 S1, PROTO-U-023), with the end note `ended`.

by.description: The person, on their own messages.

kind.description: A notice's kind (ADR-0034 S1, the notice row).

files.description: A report's files [{name, size, sha256}]; the end note's [{member, seq, name, size}] (handed back, seq being the report's).

reason.description: done, stopped (a person), budget, deadline, idle, lead_deleted or person_disabled; this list is the contract. Show a value you don't know as Stopped.

can_stop.description: Whether Stop helper would stop it now: while the team runs, any helper but a stopped one or one that couldn't start.

position.description: Its place in the queue while queued.

tokens.description: Prompt and completion tokens of its model calls since the team started, as the relay counts them; the lead's own share is budget.spent minus the helpers'.

tokens_estimated.description: Part of tokens is the relay's estimate: a model call cancelled before its server reported usage (a stop mid-reply), counted from what streamed.

tool.description: A call started and not yet ended in the step, else null (thinking or writing).

oneOf.description: done, stopped (a person), budget, deadline, idle, lead_deleted or person_disabled; this list is the contract. Show a value you don't know as Stopped.

read_seq.description: Where the lead has read to in the team's messages: the place its wake reads from (its finished runs' place, or what a run still going has read); 0 before any read.

unread.description: The team's messages after read_seq that are for the lead (to it or to the whole team), never its own: what waits unread for it, e.g. after its person stopped it.

spent.description: May pass tokens by the calls in flight when the budget ran out.

version.description: Rises with every change; team.changed names it.

member_route.description: A model route that exists and can be used now.

ScreenNotice.description: One of the gateway's screen notices (ADR-0039): never sequenced into the runtime's log, never what was typed or pasted.

name.description: The person's sign-in address, the gateway's name for a person.

by.description: The person who took over, handed back or signed out.

after_seq.description: The conversation's last stored event seq when it happened.

seconds.description: screen.handed_back only: how long Take over lasted; absent when it ended by a restart.

ended.description: screen.handed_back only: Hand back, the holder's socket closed, or the gateway restarted.

reason.description: screen.sign_out_failed only: the runtime couldn't empty the browser's profile, or never confirmed it.
